description: A Director of Patent Strategy must approve the response and continuation plan for a pending patent application, including the claims to pursue, the continuation's focus, required government-funding notice, and a chain-of-title cure, with input from patent prosecution, product, government-contracts, and IP operations specialists.

shared_context.S1: The company has a pending patent application for its automated diagnostic platform.
shared_context.S2: The application has received a non-final office action, and the response is due 28 days from today.
shared_context.S3: The current draft response would continue pursuing the application's existing claim set and would not file a continuation.
shared_context.S4: Elena approves the final prosecution plan, and the firm's routine pre-filing review requires patent prosecution, product, government-contracts, and IP operations to report any issue affecting the filing.

PF1.text: While preparing the office-action response, Theo completed a supplemental prior-art comparison showing that claims 1 through 6 are anticipated, while claim 7 remains patentable if the response narrows the prosecution track to claim 7 only; he has not yet circulated that comparison because he completed it after the response draft went to internal review.

PF2.text: Mina confirmed with the platform engineering team this week that the next commercial release depends on preserving the claim 12 improvement, which is not in the pending application's viable claim 7; the team needs a continuation focused on the claim 12 improvement, but this product requirement was recorded in a launch-planning file rather than the patent matter.

PF3.text: Caleb verified against the company's federal research grant file that the invention used grant-funded work and therefore the filing must include the exact government-funding notice required by the grant terms; he has not added the notice to the response checklist because the grant file was reviewed by government contracts rather than the patent group.

PF4.text: Nora found in the executed inventor records that one inventor's assignment omits the continuation rights needed for this patent family; before filing the continuation, the company must obtain and record a corrected assignment, and she has not raised it because the assignment repository is maintained separately from the docketing system.

acceptance_conditions: The response must narrow the prosecution track to claim 7 only.
The continuation must focus on the claim 12 improvement.
The government-funding notice required by the grant terms must be included.
A corrected inventor assignment must be obtained and recorded before the continuation is filed.
The filing plan must include an assignment-cure commitment.

decisive_facts.why: The supplemental comparison changes the response from continuing the existing claim set to pursuing claim 7 only, and supplies the prior-art fact that must be cited for that choice.
The launch requirement changes the plan from no continuation to filing one specifically focused on the claim 12 improvement.
The grant-funded origin changes the filing from omitting a funding disclosure to including the exact government-funding notice required by the grant terms.
The missing continuation rights in the inventor assignment changes the plan from filing without a title action to requiring a corrected assignment to be obtained and recorded before filing.
